newsitem.title: UK: Errant Catholic bishop branded a Judas.
newsitem.headline: Errant Catholic bishop branded a Judas.

text.p: Errant Bishop Roderick Wright was denounced on Sunday as a Judas from the pulpit of his old parish after he sold the story of his runaway romance with a divorcee to a racy British tabloid, provoking outrage among Catholics.

"Like Christ was betrayed by someone in his group for 30 pieces of silver, perhaps we feel similarly betrayed at this moment in time," Father Sean MacAulay, a priest in Wright's former parish in Oban, Scotland, told a congregation at an early morning Mass.

Wright confessed in the top-selling tabloid News of the World to loving Kathleen MacPhee, a 41-year-old divorced mother of three, and apologised for the pain he had caused to an illegitimate son he had fathered by another woman.
The scandal surrounding Wright has stunned the Catholic Church in Britain and stirred a public debate over priests' commitment to celibacy.

The reference to Judas, a disciple who betrayed Christ, followed a disclosure that Wright had been paid a reported 300,000 pound ($465,900) fee for the confession to the News of the World, a newspaper specialising in sex scandals.
Wright says the money will go to MacPhee's children.
"We regard the sale of his story by Roderick Wright as deplorable," Cardinal Thomas Winning, head of the Catholic Church in Scotland, said in a statement.

In a story splashed over five pages, Wright denied he had a sexual relationship with MacPhee but said he intended to marry her. Their relationship had started out innocently but he could no longer fight his feelings for her.

"There has been no sexual relationship between us...We have never made love to each other. We have not even shared the same bed or slept together," he said. "We tried to contain it. We spent time not seeing each other. There were long gaps."

Wright, 56, who was interviewed in a cottage where he is in hiding, said he wanted to apologise for the hurt they had caused and said he had never intended to "go missing" when he left his cathedral two weeks ago.
"We were going to start a new life together. That was my hope and plan. But it has spiralled out of control."
The former bishop also regretted the neglect and hurt he had caused to his son Kevin, the result of his relationship with another woman, Joanna Whibley.
But he denied that there had been other mistresses. "There have been no other affairs with any other women. Just these two.
Father Tom Connelly, spokesman for the Scottish Catholics Bishop's Conference, described the selling of Wright's story as "beyond belief."
"At least part of that money should go to this boy Kevin and the mother. I think it is shocking," he told Sky television news.

Wright resigned as bishop three days after he vanished with MacPhee. The church was still reeling from the scandal when Whibley felt compelled to come forward and reveal that the errant bishop was the father of her son.

She said she knew that Wright had planned to resign as bishop but she had hoped that he would come and live with her and their child. His disappearance with another women prompted her finally to reveal her guilty secret.
Footage of Kevin sobbing about his absent father on national television saying, "It's too late now. I don't even want him if he comes," added another tragic dimension to a tawdry tale.
Wright said Whibley had every right to say what she did and he wished her and their son happiness.
"I can only say I have a very guilty conscience because of the way I have treated him and because of my negligence," he told the newspaper.
"I only wish him happiness. But at this particular time I don't know how I can bring him his happiness."
Wright said his relationship with MacPhee had grown into something stronger than friendship while she was battling against cervical cancer.
MacPhee, pictured holding hands with Wright in the hideaway in northern England, said she hoped that there would be a "healing of all the hurt." ($1=.6439 Pound)
